# User Sessions

## Session overview [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#session-overview)

A session is created when a user signs in. By default, sessions last **30 days** and a user can have an unlimited number of active sessions.

A session is represented by a secure session token stored in signed HttpOnly cookies.

## Automatic session refresh [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#automatic-session-refresh)

Openfort uses a **sliding session** model:

- Sessions automatically extend when the user makes authenticated requests
- If a session is accessed within its refresh window (one day before potential refresh), the expiration extends
- No manual "refresh token" exchange is required
- If a session hasn't been accessed for 30 days, it expires

This approach balances security (sessions eventually expire) with convenience (active users stay logged in).

## Session termination [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#session-termination)

A session terminates when:

- The user clicks sign out
- The user changes their password or performs a security-sensitive action
- The session reaches its maximum lifetime (30 days without activity)
- The session is explicitly revoked

### Session token format [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#session-token-format)

Session tokens are:

- Randomly generated unique identifiers (32 characters)
- Signed using HMAC-SHA-256 with your project's secret
- Stored in secure, HttpOnly cookies with the `openfort` prefix
- Verified against Openfort's servers on each request

The token format is `{token}.{signature}`, where the signature ensures the token hasn't been tampered with.

## Authorizing requests with the session token [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#authorizing-requests-with-the-session-token)

To include the current user's session token on requests to your backend, use the `getAccessToken()` method. The SDK handles token management internally.

```
const accessToken = await openfort.getAccessToken();

const response = await fetch(<your-api-route>, {
    method: <your-request-method>
    body: <your-request-body>,
    headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        /* Add any other request headers you'd like */
    }
});
```

[Verify tokens server-side](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/server/access-token)

Verify tokens server-side

Server-side validation

Learn how to validate the access token on your backend

## Log out users [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/user-sessions\#log-out-users)

Upon sign out, the session is invalidated in the database and the client library removes the session stored in the browser.

# Updated authentication

All projects created after **January 14, 2026** use the updated authentication module (v2). Projects created before this date continue to use the original authentication module (v1).

The authentication version is permanently tied to your project and can't be changed. If you call an endpoint from the wrong version, the API returns an error. Make sure you use the endpoints and SDK versions that match your project's authentication version.

## Why there are two versions [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/updated-authentication\#why-there-are-two-versions)

Openfort introduced an updated authentication module to improve security and streamline the authentication flow. Because of this change, the API documentation splits authentication endpoints into two separate tags:

- [Auth v1 endpoints](https://openfort-xyz.github.io/swagger-api-doc/#/auth%20v1) — for projects created before January 14, 2026.
- [Auth v2 endpoints](https://openfort-xyz.github.io/swagger-api-doc/#/auth%20v2) — for projects created after January 14, 2026.

## SDK compatibility [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/updated-authentication\#sdk-compatibility)

Openfort SDKs were also updated to support the v2 authentication module. Starting from the following versions, SDKs use v2 endpoints:

| SDK | v2 starting version |
| --- | --- |
| `@openfort/openfort-js` | 1.0.0 |
| `@openfort/react-native` | 1.0.0 |
| `@openfort/react` | 0.2.0 |
| `Unity - com.openfort.sdk` | 0.4.0 |

## Determine your project version [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/updated-authentication\#determine-your-project-version)

Check your project creation date in the [Openfort dashboard](https://dashboard.openfort.io/). Projects display their creation date on the **Settings** page.

- **Created before January 14, 2026** — use v1 SDK versions and [auth v1 endpoints](https://openfort-xyz.github.io/swagger-api-doc/#/auth%20v1).
- **Created after January 14, 2026** — use the latest SDK versions and [auth v2 endpoints](https://openfort-xyz.github.io/swagger-api-doc/#/auth%20v2).

## Install Openfort with the CLI [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#install-openfort-with-the-cli)

The **Openfort CLI** helps you set up a new project with all dependencies and configurations. You can select framework (Vite or Next.js), authentication providers, embedded wallet, and UI theming.

## Install manually (step by step) [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#install-manually-step-by-step)

Starting from scratch? Create a new React app first

pnpmnpmyarn


### Install dependencies [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#install-dependencies)

Install [@openfort/react](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openfort/react) and chain-specific packages. Use the snippet for your chain:

EthereumSolana

```
pnpm add @openfort/react wagmi @tanstack/react-query viem@^2
```

```
pnpm add @openfort/react @solana/kit
```

Use `npm install ...` or `yarn add ...` if you prefer those package managers.

### Get your Openfort API keys [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#get-your-openfort-api-keys)

In the [API keys](https://dashboard.openfort.io/api-keys) section of the [Openfort dashboard](https://dashboard.openfort.io/):

- **Publishable Key**: Safe for client-side use
- **Secret Key**: Server-side only

To generate non-custodial wallets:

1. Scroll to the Shield section and click **Create Shield keys**
2. **Store the encryption share** safely when it appears (you'll only see it once)
3. You'll receive **Shield Publishable Key** and **Shield Secret Key**

### Choose your recovery method [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#choose-your-recovery-method)

Decide which wallet recovery experience you want to ship:

- **Automatic recovery** — no action from the user required. **Solana uses this by default**; for Ethereum you can choose it and set up a backend endpoint.
- [Passkey recovery](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react/quickstart/passkey#choose-your-recovery-method) — biometric or device authentication with no backend endpoint.
- [Password recovery](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react/quickstart/password#choose-your-recovery-method) — user sets their own password with no backend endpoint.

### Set up the recovery endpoint [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#set-up-the-recovery-endpoint)

Required for **Automatic recovery**. Create a backend endpoint that returns a Shield encryption session. See [setting up the recovery endpoint](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/server/automatic-recovery-session).

**One-click deploy:**

[![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/openfort-xyz/recovery-endpoint-cloudflare)

[![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https://github.com/openfort-xyz/recovery-endpoint-vercel&project-name=shield-recovery-endpoint&env=SHIELD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY,SHIELD_SECRET_KEY,SHIELD_ENCRYPTION_SHARE&envDescription=Required%20Shield%20API%20keys%20from%20your%20Openfort%20project&envLink=https://www.openfort.io/docs)

**Or implement your own:** expose a POST endpoint that returns `{ "session": "<session_id>" }`. See the [backend repo](https://github.com/openfort-xyz/openfort-backend-quickstart) for examples.

Save your endpoint URL for the next step (e.g. `https://your-domain.com/api/protected-create-encryption-session`).

### Set up providers [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#set-up-providers)

Wrap your app with the appropriate providers for your chain.

## Providers.tsx [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#providerstsx)

EthereumSolana

```
import React from "react";
import { AuthProvider, OpenfortProvider, RecoveryMethod } from "@openfort/react";
import { getDefaultConfig, OpenfortWagmiBridge } from "@openfort/react/wagmi";
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { WagmiProvider, createConfig } from "wagmi";
import { baseSepolia } from "viem/chains";

const config = createConfig(
  getDefaultConfig({
    appName: "Openfort Demo App",
    chains: [baseSepolia],
    ssr: true,
  })
);

const queryClient = new QueryClient();

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <WagmiProvider config={config}>
        <OpenfortWagmiBridge>
          <OpenfortProvider
            publishableKey="YOUR_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY"
            walletConfig={{
              shieldPublishableKey: "YOUR_OPENFORT_SHIELD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY",
              ethereum: { chainId: 84532 },
              createEncryptedSessionEndpoint: "https://your-domain.com/api/protected-create-encryption-session",
            }}
            uiConfig={{
              authProviders: [AuthProvider.EMAIL_OTP, AuthProvider.GUEST],
              walletRecovery: { defaultMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC },
            }}
          >
            {children}
          </OpenfortProvider>
        </OpenfortWagmiBridge>
      </WagmiProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

```
        publishableKey="YOUR_OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY"
        walletConfig={{
          shieldPublishableKey: "YOUR_OPENFORT_SHIELD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY",
          solana: { cluster: "devnet" },
          createEncryptedSessionEndpoint: "https://your-domain.com/api/protected-create-encryption-session",
        }}
        uiConfig={{
          authProviders: [AuthProvider.EMAIL_OTP, AuthProvider.GUEST],
          walletRecovery: { defaultMethod: RecoveryMethod.AUTOMATIC },
```

Add `walletConnectProjectId` to `getDefaultConfig`. Get a project ID from the [WalletConnect dashboard](https://cloud.reown.com/sign-in).

### You're good to go! [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#youre-good-to-go)

Wrap your app in `Providers` and add the Openfort button:

App.tsx

```
import React from "react";
import { Providers } from "./Providers";
import { OpenfortButton } from "@openfort/react";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Providers>
      <OpenfortButton />
    </Providers>
  );
}
```

## Advanced provider props [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#advanced-provider-props)

`OpenfortProvider` also accepts these optional props:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overrides` | `SDKOverrides` | Override SDK internals (advanced). |
| `onConnect` | `({ address, connectorId, user }) => void` | Callback fired when a wallet connects. Receives the connected address, connector ID, and user object. |
| `onDisconnect` | `() => void` | Callback fired when a wallet disconnects. |
| `thirdPartyAuth` | `ThirdPartyAuthConfiguration` | Configuration for third-party authentication providers. |
| `walletConfig.connectOnLogin` | `boolean` | Whether to automatically recover/create a wallet after authentication. Set inside `walletConfig`, not as a direct provider prop. Defaults to `true`. |

## Utility exports [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/react\#utility-exports)

`@openfort/react` also exports the following utility functions:

- `createSIWEMessage` — Create a SIWE (Sign-In with Ethereum) message for custom authentication flows.
- `formatAddress` — Format a wallet address for display (truncation, checksumming).
- `getDefaultSolanaRpcUrl` — Get the default Solana RPC URL for a given cluster.
- `invalidateBalance` — Invalidate cached balance data to trigger a refresh.

# Using a third-party auth provider

Openfort's signer solution enables user onboarding by integrating with backend solutions and authentication providers that support JWT-based authentication.

## Third-party auth platforms [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth\#third-party-auth-platforms)

With this approach, Openfort creates **embedded wallets** on the client and follows the necessary security steps to ensure the smart wallet remains non-custodial.

- **[PlayFab](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/playfab)**
- **[Firebase](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/firebase)**
- **[Better-Auth](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/better-auth)**
- **[Accelbyte](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/accelbyte)**
- **[Lootlocker](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/lootlocker)**
- **[Supabase](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth/supabase)**

## Custom auth methods [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/external-auth\#custom-auth-methods)

Openfort offers two options to set up embedded signers with custom auth: one based on the [OpenID Connect](https://openid.net/developers/how-connect-works/) (OIDC) standard, and a generic option that lets you bring your own auth server.

- **[Custom OIDC Token](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/custom-auth/oidc-token)**
- **[Custom Auth Token](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/custom-auth/auth-token)**

# Custom OIDC auth

OIDC authentication is a viable choice when using an external authentication provider such as Auth0 or Cognito that offers JWK publication for token authenticity verification.

An OIDC authentication framework employs a public-private key pair, utilizing the private key to sign authentication tokens. The public key is made accessible via a public URL in JWKS format, typically found at `https://{domain}.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. When a user logs in, an idToken (a JWT) is produced and signed with the private key, following OIDC specifications for token field requirements. This JWT is then used within the private key to create a user wallet.

The verification of the JWT against the public key confirms its authenticity, allowing wallet generation based on the subject (user identifier) within the idToken.

## Input requirements [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/custom-auth/oidc-token\#input-requirements)

- **JWKS File URL (public key):** Validates the token's authentic signature
- **idToken's `aud` value:** Confirms that the intended recipient of the token is correct

## Authenticating users with OIDC-compatible authentication [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/custom-auth/oidc-token\#authenticating-users-with-oidc-compatible-authentication)

### Set up your provider [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/configuration/custom-auth/oidc-token\#set-up-your-provider)

To set up your OIDC Authentication with Openfort, visit your [dashboard provider settings](https://dashboard.openfort.io/providers).

# User session and authorization

## Get a user's session token from a request [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/server/access-token\#get-a-users-session-token-from-a-request)

When your app frontend sends a request to your server, include the current user's session token in the Authorization header. This allows your backend to securely identify the requesting user and gate API routes based on their authentication status, user ID, and more.

When your server receives a request, the location of the user's session token depends on whether your app uses local storage (the default) or cookies to manage user sessions:

- If using **local storage** to store a user's session, the session token is passed in the Authorization header of the request.
- If using **cookies** to store a user's session, the session token is passed in the `openfort.session_token` cookie on the request.

For example, in [NextJS](https://nextjs.org/), you might extract the session token from a `NextApiRequest` as follows:

## Verify the user's session token [Link to this section](https://www.openfort.io/docs/products/embedded-wallet/server/access-token\#verify-the-users-session-token)

Once you've obtained the user's session token from a request, verify the token against Openfort to confirm that Openfort issued it and the user referenced by the token is authenticated.

Session tokens are signed using HMAC-SHA-256 and verified against Openfort's servers. Use the official Openfort Node SDK to verify tokens:

Node.js

```
import Openfort from "@openfort/openfort-node";
const openfort = new Openfort(process.env.OPENFORT_SK, {
  publishableKey: process.env.OPENFORT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY,
});

const session = await openfort.iam.getSession({ accessToken: "USER_SESSION_TOKEN" });
console.log("User ID:", session.user.id);
console.log("User Email:", session.user.email);
console.log("Session expires:", session.session.expiresAt);
```

The `getSession` method validates the token signature and checks that the session hasn't expired (sessions last 30 days by default with automatic refresh on activity).

BEGIN;

CREATE TYPE user_type AS ENUM ('individual', 'company');
CREATE TYPE user_role AS ENUM ('admin', 'moderator', 'support','project_owner', 'investor', 'contractor', 'governance');
CREATE TYPE user_status AS ENUM ('active', 'inactive', 'suspended', 'pending_kyc');

CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    particle_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE,

    first_name VARCHAR(100),
    last_name VARCHAR(100),
    phone_number VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE,
    company_name VARCHAR(255),

    -- Verification
    kyc_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    kyc_verified_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    kyb_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    kyb_verified_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    -- User classification
    type user_type NOT NULL,
    role user_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'investor',
    status user_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending_kyc',

    -- GDPR
    data_deletion_requested_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    data_deletion_scheduled_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,

    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
);

CREATE INDEX idx_users_particle_id ON users(particle_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_phone_number ON users(phone_number);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_type ON users(type);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_role ON users(role);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_status ON users(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_created_at ON users(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_updated_at ON users(updated_at);

CREATE TABLE wallets (
    user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    chain VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    public_address VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,

    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chain, public_address)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_wallets_chain ON wallets(chain);
CREATE INDEX idx_wallets_public_address ON wallets(public_address);
CREATE INDEX idx_wallets_created_at ON wallets(created_at);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    -- Opaque token hashed for security
    refresh_token_hash BYTEA UNIQUE NOT NULL,

    user_agent TEXT,
    ip_address TEXT,
    platform VARCHAR(50),      -- 'web', 'mobile', 'desktop'
    browser VARCHAR(100),
    device VARCHAR(100),

    is_trusted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,  -- Device remembered?

    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    last_activity_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    activity_timeout_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,

        CHECK (absolute_expires_at > created_at),

    CONSTRAINT revocation_consistency

    WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_absolute_expires

    WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_revoked_at
    ON sessions(revoked_at DESC) -- Order by most recently revoked

**Considering authentication endpoints**

I think to minimize changes, I can keep `POST /v1/auth/login` but implement the Openfort Bearer token. For `POST /v1/auth/register`, I’ll use it only if extra fields are needed. The user prefers a cleanup and no migration. From the frontend perspective, the simplest approach is to create a single exchange endpoint after Openfort login, possibly named `/v1/auth/openfort/exchange`. This keeps things explicit without complicating the login and register functions. I need to ensure this is consistent in the backend documentation.**Validating authentication tokens**

I plan to validate the token against the Openfort server using something like `getSession`. This will help me extract the `session.user.id`, `email`, and `phone`. Then, I can upsert the local user data upon the first sign-in. I’ll need to return the current app JWT access token along with a refresh cookie and possibly some user payload data. Also, I should note that there won't be a Next.js auth proxy; instead, I’ll call `backpro` directly from the browser with `credentials: 'include'`.**Considering wallet table population**

I’m thinking about how not to block login during wallet table population. It seems like we can either leave the wallet table untouched or sync it later. During the first sign-in, I should auto-provision a local user with the necessary defaults for the current schema, but I need to specify the defaults properly. Since there's no onboarding form, I'm leaning towards making the `type` nullable or defaulting to `individual`, with other roles set as well. However, if there's a chance that KYC or organization flow matters, I might need to rethink this to avoid misclassifying organization users.**Evaluating schema changes**

I’m considering how to adapt the schema since the frontend no longer collects the `type` on login. It seems the best approach might be to make `type` nullable or set it to an explicit `unknown` until an onboarding process is in place, while defaulting the role to `investor`. However, adding `unknown` to the enum can be more complicated. Maybe a simpler solution would be to add an enum value for `'unknown'` instead. I don’t want to overcomplicate things!**Simplifying user schema**

I'm considering the current user schema and how it can be simplified since there aren't any existing users and no registration flow. I think making `type` nullable and not embedding it in the JWT until onboarding could work, but this might involve bigger changes to the auth middleware. 

The user asked for a complete plan, so recommending a schema simplification is crucial. We could rename `particle_id` to `openfort_user_id` and introduce an `unknown` enum for `type`, as the current frontend collects none. It might be worth inspecting the domain user object enums for possibilities.

# v0.2.1 Openfort Implementation Part 2

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Status:** Approved plan
**Predecessor:** `docs-dev/audit-review/v0.2.0-openfort-integration-review-1.md`

## Goal

Finish the Openfort migration in `front-pro` as part of a coordinated frontend + backend move away from Particle.

## Current State

- Openfort provider wiring is structurally correct.
- `/login` uses `OpenfortButton`.
- Automatic recovery endpoint is present.
- Legacy guest header, wallet modal, and bearer-token utilities still exist and remain active in the main app.
- `backpro` already has JWT/session infrastructure, but its auth contract is still Particle-based.
- The live frontend no longer collects the old backend registration fields (`uuid`, `token`, role/type/profile form data), so the next backend contract must work from Openfort session state first and app-profile completion second.

## Selected Direction

- **Option B selected:** coordinated `front-pro` + `backpro` migration
- **Frontend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Backend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Frontend route policy:** all non-`/login` pages are treated as authenticated app pages
- **Wallet UX policy:** use Openfort stock UI/modal, remove custom wallet/login flow from the live path
- **External wallet policy:** keep WalletConnect / MetaMask support in the provider config; reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in a dedicated external-wallet phase
- **Greenfield policy:** there are no legacy users to migrate, so the Openfort branches may make contract/schema breaking changes instead of preserving the old Particle login shape

## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context

- This repo is the frontend half of the migration.
- The backend half lives in the sibling repo: `../backpro`
- Frontend task document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- Backend companion document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories, not from `develop`.

## Branch Strategy

### `front-pro`

1. Preserve the current Openfort work on branch `openfort`
2. Recreate `develop` from commit `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`
3. Use `develop` as the Particle-era fallback line
4. Continue all Openfort migration work on `openfort`

### `backpro`

1. Create branch `openfort` from current `develop`
2. Leave `develop` unchanged
3. Continue all Openfort backend migration work on `openfort`

## Current Frontend Surfaces Treated As Authenticated

These routes currently exist in `src/app` and should be treated as app/private surfaces in this phase unless intentionally split later:

- `/`
- `/home`
- `/explore-projects`
- `/create-project`
- `/tokenization`
- `/investment-portal`
- `/digital-assets`
- `/investor-management`
- `/investment-requests`
- `/asset-management`
- `/swap`
- `/kyc`

Public/auth exception:

- `/login`

## Target Outcome

1. Users authenticate through Openfort and remain authenticated across the app.
2. Protected app routes in `front-pro` respect auth state.
3. The header and wallet entry points use Openfort state/components instead of legacy mock flows.
4. Backend API access is aligned with an Openfort-compatible backend session model.
5. The app exposes a clear sign-in / sign-out / connected-wallet experience.
6. `backpro` preserves its JWT/refresh/session architecture while replacing Particle as the identity source.

## Concrete Frontend ↔ Backend Contract For This Phase

Use a dedicated backend session-exchange endpoint instead of reviving the old Particle login/register proxies:

- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - frontend sends `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
  - token source is `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
  - request body is optional and should only carry app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - uses the existing backend refresh-cookie flow
- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - revokes backend refresh session
- `GET /v1/me`
  - returns the backend user/profile/session view for the authenticated app shell

Recommended frontend behavior:

- after Openfort login succeeds, exchange the Openfort token for an InfraFund backend session
- keep the returned backend access token in memory, not `localStorage`
- call `backpro` directly from the browser with `credentials: 'include'`
- keep only the Openfort Shield recovery route in Next.js; do not keep the old auth proxy layer alive just to preserve Particle-era paths

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Repository preparation

- Keep active work on `openfort` in both repositories
- Update this task document to reflect the approved coordinated plan
- Create a backend-specific task document under `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/`

### Phase 2 — App-wide frontend auth integration

- Use the `useUser()` hook from `@openfort/react` as the primary auth-state source
- Implement a **client-side layout guard** (not `middleware.ts`) since Openfort session state is SDK-based and not available server-side
- Redirect authenticated users away from `/login`
- Guard app routes so unauthenticated users are redirected to `/login`
- Add loading/fallback handling while Openfort resolves session state
- Treat the existing app-shell pages as private surfaces unless intentionally split into public pages later
- Remove `AuthProvider.WALLET` from the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` (will be reintroduced in the external wallet phase)

### Phase 3 — Replace the live legacy wallet UX

- Remove or retire `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx` from the header flow
- Replace the header wallet action with Openfort-native behavior:
  - `OpenfortButton`
  - Openfort stock modal/profile flow
- Ensure the live wallet entry point is consistent with the login experience

### Phase 4 — User identity and sign-out

- Replace hardcoded guest text in `src/components/header.tsx`
- Show user identity from Openfort state
- Confirm the stock Openfort account flow covers sign-out behavior cleanly
- Confirm the post-sign-out redirect and app state reset

### Phase 5 — Frontend legacy auth cleanup

**Keep (Openfort-native):**

- `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` — Shield recovery endpoint, already integrated

**Review and either integrate or remove these legacy paths:**

- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts` — reads token from `localStorage`; replace with Openfort JWT from `useUser()` / SDK auth state
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts` — attaches `Authorization` header; rework to source tokens from Openfort session instead of `localStorage`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`
- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/deposit/route.ts`

Recommended cleanup decision for this phase:

- **Keep**
  - `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts`
- **Delete now (currently unused legacy Particle/BFF paths)**
  - `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/deposit/route.ts`
  - `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
  - `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
  - `src/utils/axios.utils.ts`
  - `src/services/api.service.ts`

Reason: the listed files are unused and still encode the dead Particle/localStorage/proxy contract. New backend calls should be rebuilt around the Openfort exchange endpoint and direct browser → `backpro` requests.

### Phase 6 — Backend auth migration dependency

- `backpro` keeps its JWT/refresh/session architecture
- Replace Particle-specific auth inputs and validation
- Stop depending on `ParticleID` as the long-term auth identity key
- Replace it with a unique `openfort_user_id` key sourced from the validated Openfort session
- Validate the Openfort access token server-side against Openfort before issuing InfraFund JWTs
- Adopt the exchange endpoint described above as the single frontend → backend auth handshake
- Add first authenticated backend surfaces such as `/me` and account/KYC status

### Phase 7 — External wallet support (WalletConnect / MetaMask)

- Reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
- Verify WalletConnect project ID is configured and the connect flow works end-to-end
- Test MetaMask and other external wallet connections via `OpenfortWagmiBridge`
- Ensure external-wallet sessions integrate cleanly with the auth guard and header identity flow

### Phase 8 — Config hardening

- Keep Shield recovery and current Openfort provider stack
- Keep WalletConnect support wired via optional env var (`NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID`)
- Confirm target chains and sponsorship behavior for Base / Base Sepolia
- Verify environment-variable naming and required runtime fallbacks

### Phase 9 — Validation

- Run validators in both repositories after doc and code changes
- Run lint, typecheck, prettier, and targeted runtime verification in `front-pro`
- Run the relevant backend checks in `backpro`
- Manually verify:
  - login
  - redirect behavior
  - wallet creation/recovery
  - sign-out
  - header/account state
  - first backend-authenticated account flow kept in scope

## Suggested File Touch List

- `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
- `src/components/auth/login.tsx`
- `src/components/header.tsx`
- `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`
- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- route/layout files needed for auth guards

## Existing Frontend Files That Show The Old Contract

These are the clearest handoff pointers for where the old backend/Particle-era assumptions still leak into the frontend:

- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`

All of the above should be treated as removal candidates unless a new Openfort-based backend call path explicitly replaces them.

## Backend Dependency Summary

`backpro` already has:

- JWT access tokens
- refresh-token cookie flow
- auth middleware
- session / lockout logic
- tests and clean layering

But it is still provider-bound to Particle:

- login/register expect `uuid` + `token`
- auth service calls `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- users are keyed around `ParticleID`
- wallet creation depends on Particle user info

Current backend auth endpoints in active `backpro` routing:

- `/v1/auth/register`
- `/v1/auth/login`
- `/v1/auth/refresh`
- `/v1/auth/logout`

So the backend effort is not “build auth from scratch”; it is “swap the identity source while preserving the existing session architecture.”

## Related PR Notes

### PR #18

- Relevant to later KYC work
- Contains useful Sumsub / applicant groundwork
- Not merge-ready and should be treated as selective reference material, not merged blindly during auth migration

### PR #22

- Not relevant to the Openfort migration
- Only addresses a scheduler test race condition

## Validation / Environment Notes

- `front-pro` validators are green for the current doc state:
  - `npm run format`
  - `tsc --noEmit`
- `backpro` currently does **not** have a clean full test run in this local environment even before migration work because:
  - generated package `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/gen` is missing
  - `tests/mocks` is missing
  - there is also a `sonic` build issue in the current environment
- Any future engineer picking this up should treat those `backpro` issues as baseline environment/setup blockers, not as Openfort-migration regressions.

## Decisions Needed Before Implementation

The key product/architecture decisions for this phase have been made:

1. Option B is selected
2. Openfort stock UI is selected
3. External wallets are not required in this phase
4. Current app-shell pages are treated as authenticated pages
5. There is no legacy-user migration requirement
6. Legacy Next.js auth proxy routes should be deleted rather than adapted
7. Frontend should use `useUser().getAccessToken()` + backend session exchange, not `localStorage`

## Can implementation start now?

**Yes.**

The next execution order is:

1. repository preparation
2. frontend auth completion on `front-pro/openfort`
3. backend auth migration on `backpro/openfort`
4. selective KYC follow-up later

## Recommended First Code Pass After This Doc

1. `front-pro`: finish route guarding and replace the header wallet path with Openfort stock UI
2. `front-pro`: remove or isolate the old token/proxy plumbing
3. `backpro`: replace Particle-specific auth input + identity lookup
4. `backpro`: add `/me` and account/KYC-status endpoints
5. wire the new frontend/backend handshake together

# v0.2.1 Openfort Backend Migration Part 1

**Date:** 2026-03-27  
**Status:** Approved plan  
**Frontend companion:** `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`

## Goal

Migrate `backpro` from Particle-based authentication to an Openfort-compatible backend session model while preserving the existing JWT, refresh-token, and middleware architecture.

## Current Backend Reality

`backpro` already has a good authentication foundation:

- JWT access token generation
- refresh-token cookie flow
- auth middleware
- session and lockout handling
- tests and clean layering

But it is still tied to Particle:

- login/register inputs expect `uuid` + `token`
- auth service calls `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- users are keyed around `ParticleID`
- wallet creation depends on Particle user info

## Selected Direction

- Create and use branch `openfort`
- Preserve the existing session architecture
- Replace Particle as the identity/auth provider
- Add a minimal protected API surface needed by the frontend
- Treat PR #18 as selective reference material for later KYC work
- There are no legacy users to migrate, so the backend may make direct schema/contract changes on `openfort` instead of preserving Particle compatibility

## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context

- This repo is the backend half of the migration.
- The frontend half lives in the sibling repo: `../front-pro`
- Backend task document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- Frontend companion document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories.

## Current Branch Policy

- `backpro/openfort` is the branch of record for backend migration work
- `backpro/develop` remains the pre-Openfort backend line
- `front-pro/openfort` is the branch of record for frontend migration work
- `front-pro/develop` was intentionally reset to the Particle-era fallback point `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`

## Current Active Auth Contract

Current routed auth endpoints in `backpro`:

- `/v1/auth/register`
- `/v1/auth/login`
- `/v1/auth/refresh`
- `/v1/auth/logout`

Current request/response behavior:

- register/login expect Particle-style `uuid` + `token`
- successful login returns:
  - JWT `access_token`
  - refresh-token cookie

## Recommended Replacement Auth Contract

Replace the Particle pair (`uuid` + `token`) with a single Openfort session-token exchange:

- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - required header: `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
  - token is sourced on the frontend from `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
  - optional body: only app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - unchanged in purpose; continues to mint a new InfraFund access token from the refresh cookie
- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - unchanged in purpose; revokes the InfraFund session
- `GET /v1/me`
  - first authenticated read endpoint for the app shell

Validation rule for `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`:

- do not trust frontend-supplied user IDs or emails
- verify the presented Openfort access token against Openfort server-side first
- derive the durable external identity from the validated Openfort session response (`user.id`)
- then create or look up the local InfraFund user and issue the existing InfraFund JWT + refresh cookie

Official Openfort guidance for server-side validation points to session verification via Openfort's server APIs (`getSession`). Since `backpro` is Go, implement an Openfort adapter in Go that performs the same server-side session validation over HTTPS; do not rely on client-side JWT parsing alone.

## Primary Backend Entry Points To Rework

These are the most important implementation handoff files:

- `internal/interfaces/rest/router/auth.go`
- `internal/interfaces/rest/handler/auth.go`
- `internal/interfaces/rest/input/auth.go`
- `internal/application/auth/auth.go`
- `internal/application/auth/auth_helpers.go`
- `internal/application/auth/dto/login.go`
- `internal/application/auth/dto/registeration.go`
- `internal/domain/user/entity/user.go`
- `internal/domain/user/repository/user.go`
- `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/user_repo.go`
- `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/queries/user.sql`

Particle-specific anchors to remove or redesign:

- `ParticleID` field on user entities / persistence
- `GetByParticleID(...)`
- `ExistsParticleID(...)`
- `particle.GetUserInfo(...)` in auth service
- wallet creation during auth based on Particle wallet payloads

## Target Outcome

1. `backpro` no longer depends on Particle for login/register
2. `backpro` still issues JWT access tokens and refresh-token cookies
3. The frontend can exchange Openfort-authenticated identity for an InfraFund app session
4. The backend exposes first authenticated endpoints such as `/me` and account/KYC status
5. Future KYC work can build on a stable post-Particle auth model

## Greenfield Schema Decision

Because there are no existing users to migrate:

- rename/replace `particle_id` with `openfort_user_id` as the unique durable identity key
- remove `GetByParticleID(...)` / `ExistsParticleID(...)` repository methods in favor of Openfort equivalents
- delete Particle-specific DTO fields from login/register handlers
- allow the schema and endpoint contract to break cleanly on `openfort`

Because the current frontend no longer collects a registration profile before login:

- first successful Openfort exchange should auto-provision a minimal local user
- use `openfort_user_id` as the only required external identity
- default role to `investor`
- default status to `pending_kyc`
- either make `type` nullable or supply a temporary default during auto-provisioning; do not keep auth blocked on the old Particle-era registration payload

For this branch, the recommended choice is to simplify the schema enough for auto-provisioning instead of recreating a separate registration form before users can enter the app.

## Wallet Data Decision

Do not preserve the old Particle behavior where backend auth creates wallet rows as part of login/register.

- Openfort owns wallet lifecycle
- wallet balances/pages are expected to read directly from chain/Openfort client state in the frontend
- backend auth should not fail just because no wallet sync occurred
- any wallet persistence in `backpro` should be a later sync concern, not a prerequisite for authentication

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Define the new auth contract

- Replace the Particle-specific auth input contract
- Use `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>` as the proof of identity sent from the frontend
- Validate that token against Openfort server-side before issuing InfraFund credentials
- Keep the backend-issued session model rather than making the frontend trust-only
- Add `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange` as the new entry point

### Phase 2 — Replace Particle-bound auth logic

- Remove auth service dependency on `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- Replace `ParticleID`-centric lookup / registration assumptions
- Use `openfort_user_id` as the durable user identity key and mapping strategy
- Stop requiring Particle wallet payloads during auth

### Phase 3 — Preserve and adapt existing session architecture

- Keep JWT access token generation
- Keep refresh-token cookie flow
- Keep auth middleware and session management
- Rework only the identity acquisition and validation layer

### Phase 4 — Add minimal authenticated API surface

- Add `/me` or equivalent current-account endpoint
- Add basic account-status endpoint(s)
- Add KYC status endpoint(s) if that is the first protected product need

At the time of writing, those account/KYC surfaces are not present in the active router and must be added explicitly.

### Phase 5 — Frontend handshake integration

- Align the new backend auth contract with the `front-pro` Openfort flow
- Expect the frontend to send the Openfort access token obtained from `useUser().getAccessToken()`
- Expect the frontend to call `backpro` directly with `credentials: 'include'`
- Replace the old frontend proxy assumptions that expected Particle-era backend auth

### Phase 6 — KYC follow-up

- Review PR #18 selectively
- Reuse only the parts that fit the new auth contract cleanly
- Do not merge the PR wholesale without additional review

## PR Notes

### PR #18

- open draft PR
- useful Sumsub / applicant groundwork
- not merge-ready
- relevant later, not a direct Openfort auth solution
- status from review: draft + dirty, so treat it as source material, not a merge target during auth migration

Useful parts of PR #18 to revisit later:

- Sumsub adapter groundwork
- applicant service / persistence groundwork
- KYC applicant migration work

But note: active router integration for those KYC flows does not appear to be merged into the current branch line.

### PR #22

- unrelated to Openfort migration
- scheduler test race-condition fix only

## Expected Areas to Touch

- auth input / DTO definitions
- auth service and related tests
- user identity mapping logic
- Openfort session-validation adapter/client
- middleware / session integration points as needed
- first authenticated account endpoints
- docs for the new auth contract

## Validation / Environment Notes

- A full local `go test ./...` run is currently **not clean in this environment**, for reasons that appear pre-existing and unrelated to this documentation work:
  - missing generated package `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/gen`
  - missing `tests/mocks`
  - `sonic` build issue in the current environment
- Treat those as baseline setup blockers to resolve before or during backend implementation.

## Effort Estimate

- backend auth migration only: roughly **3–5 focused days**
- add first protected account endpoints: **+2–3 days**
- selective KYC follow-up from PR #18: **additional several days to ~1 week**

## Execution Order

1. establish backend planning docs
2. migrate auth contract away from Particle
3. add minimal protected account endpoints
4. integrate with `front-pro`
5. evaluate KYC follow-up from PR #18

## Recommended First Code Pass After This Doc

1. add an Openfort session-validation adapter and `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
2. replace `particle_id` with `openfort_user_id` through entity/repository/sql layers
3. remove wallet creation from the auth path
4. preserve JWT + refresh-cookie issuance
5. add `/me` endpoint
6. add account/KYC status endpoint(s)
7. wire the new contract into `front-pro/openfort`

# v0.2.1 Openfort Implementation Part 2

**Date:** 2026-03-27
**Status:** Approved plan
**Predecessor:** `docs-dev/audit-review/v0.2.0-openfort-integration-review-1.md`

## Goal

Finish the Openfort migration in `front-pro` as part of a coordinated frontend + backend move away from Particle.

## Current State

- Openfort provider wiring is structurally correct.
- `/login` uses `OpenfortButton`.
- Automatic recovery endpoint is present.
- Legacy guest header, wallet modal, and bearer-token utilities still exist and remain active in the main app.
- `backpro` already has JWT/session infrastructure, but its auth contract is still Particle-based.
- The live frontend no longer collects the old backend registration fields (`uuid`, `token`, role/type/profile form data), so the next backend contract must work from Openfort session state first and app-profile completion second.

## Selected Direction

- **Option B selected:** coordinated `front-pro` + `backpro` migration
- **Frontend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Backend branch of record:** `openfort`
- **Frontend route policy:** all non-`/login` pages are treated as authenticated app pages
- **Wallet UX policy:** use Openfort stock UI/modal, remove custom wallet/login flow from the live path
- **External wallet policy:** keep WalletConnect / MetaMask support in the provider config; reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in a dedicated external-wallet phase
- **Greenfield policy:** there are no legacy users to migrate, so the Openfort branches may make contract/schema breaking changes instead of preserving the old Particle login shape

## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context

- This repo is the frontend half of the migration.
- The backend half lives in the sibling repo: `../backpro`
- Frontend task document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- Backend companion document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories, not from `develop`.

## Branch Strategy

### `front-pro`

1. Preserve the current Openfort work on branch `openfort`
2. Recreate `develop` from commit `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`
3. Use `develop` as the Particle-era fallback line
4. Continue all Openfort migration work on `openfort`

### `backpro`

1. Create branch `openfort` from current `develop`
2. Leave `develop` unchanged
3. Continue all Openfort backend migration work on `openfort`

## Current Frontend Surfaces Treated As Authenticated

These routes currently exist in `src/app` and should be treated as app/private surfaces in this phase unless intentionally split later:

- `/`
- `/home`
- `/explore-projects`
- `/create-project`
- `/tokenization`
- `/investment-portal`
- `/digital-assets`
- `/investor-management`
- `/investment-requests`
- `/asset-management`
- `/swap`
- `/kyc`

Public/auth exception:

- `/login`

## Target Outcome

1. Users authenticate through Openfort and remain authenticated across the app.
2. Protected app routes in `front-pro` respect auth state.
3. The header and wallet entry points use Openfort state/components instead of legacy mock flows.
4. Backend API access is aligned with an Openfort-compatible backend session model.
5. The app exposes a clear sign-in / sign-out / connected-wallet experience.
6. `backpro` preserves its JWT/refresh/session architecture while replacing Particle as the identity source.

## Concrete Frontend ↔ Backend Contract For This Phase

Use a dedicated backend session-exchange endpoint instead of reviving the old Particle login/register proxies:

- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - frontend sends `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
  - token source is `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
  - request body is optional and should only carry app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - uses the existing backend refresh-cookie flow
- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - revokes backend refresh session
- `GET /v1/me`
  - returns the backend user/profile/session view for the authenticated app shell

Recommended frontend behavior:

- after Openfort login succeeds, exchange the Openfort token for an InfraFund backend session
- keep the returned backend access token in memory, not `localStorage`
- call `backpro` directly from the browser with `credentials: 'include'`
- keep only the Openfort Shield recovery route in Next.js; do not keep the old auth proxy layer alive just to preserve Particle-era paths

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Repository preparation

- Keep active work on `openfort` in both repositories
- Update this task document to reflect the approved coordinated plan
- Create a backend-specific task document under `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/`

### Phase 2 — App-wide frontend auth integration

- Use the `useUser()` hook from `@openfort/react` as the primary auth-state source
- Implement a **client-side layout guard** (not `middleware.ts`) since Openfort session state is SDK-based and not available server-side
- Redirect authenticated users away from `/login`
- Guard app routes so unauthenticated users are redirected to `/login`
- Add loading/fallback handling while Openfort resolves session state
- Treat the existing app-shell pages as private surfaces unless intentionally split into public pages later
- Remove `AuthProvider.WALLET` from the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx` (will be reintroduced in the external wallet phase)

### Phase 3 — Replace the live legacy wallet UX

- Remove or retire `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx` from the header flow
- Replace the header wallet action with Openfort-native behavior:
  - `OpenfortButton`
  - Openfort stock modal/profile flow
- Ensure the live wallet entry point is consistent with the login experience

### Phase 4 — User identity and sign-out

- Replace hardcoded guest text in `src/components/header.tsx`
- Show user identity from Openfort state
- Confirm the stock Openfort account flow covers sign-out behavior cleanly
- Confirm the post-sign-out redirect and app state reset

### Phase 5 — Frontend legacy auth cleanup

**Keep (Openfort-native):**

- `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts` — Shield recovery endpoint, already integrated

**Review and either integrate or remove these legacy paths:**

- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts` — reads token from `localStorage`; replace with Openfort JWT from `useUser()` / SDK auth state
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts` — attaches `Authorization` header; rework to source tokens from Openfort session instead of `localStorage`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`
- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/deposit/route.ts`

Recommended cleanup decision for this phase:

- **Keep**
  - `src/app/api/auth/encryption-session/route.ts`
- **Delete now (currently unused legacy Particle/BFF paths)**
  - `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
  - `src/app/api/deposit/route.ts`
  - `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
  - `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
  - `src/utils/axios.utils.ts`
  - `src/services/api.service.ts`

Reason: the listed files are unused and still encode the dead Particle/localStorage/proxy contract. New backend calls should be rebuilt around the Openfort exchange endpoint and direct browser → `backpro` requests.

### Phase 6 — Backend auth migration dependency

- `backpro` keeps its JWT/refresh/session architecture
- Replace Particle-specific auth inputs and validation
- Stop depending on `ParticleID` as the long-term auth identity key
- Replace it with a unique `openfort_user_id` key sourced from the validated Openfort session
- Validate the Openfort access token server-side against Openfort before issuing InfraFund JWTs
- Adopt the exchange endpoint described above as the single frontend → backend auth handshake
- Add first authenticated backend surfaces such as `/me` and account/KYC status

### Phase 7 — External wallet support (WalletConnect / MetaMask)

- Reintroduce `AuthProvider.WALLET` in the `authProviders` list in `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
- Verify WalletConnect project ID is configured and the connect flow works end-to-end
- Test MetaMask and other external wallet connections via `OpenfortWagmiBridge`
- Ensure external-wallet sessions integrate cleanly with the auth guard and header identity flow

### Phase 8 — Config hardening

- Keep Shield recovery and current Openfort provider stack
- Keep WalletConnect support wired via optional env var (`NEXT_PUBLIC_WALLET_CONNECT_PROJECT_ID`)
- Confirm target chains and sponsorship behavior for Base / Base Sepolia
- Verify environment-variable naming and required runtime fallbacks

### Phase 9 — Validation

- Run validators in both repositories after doc and code changes
- Run lint, typecheck, prettier, and targeted runtime verification in `front-pro`
- Run the relevant backend checks in `backpro`
- Manually verify:
  - login
  - redirect behavior
  - wallet creation/recovery
  - sign-out
  - header/account state
  - first backend-authenticated account flow kept in scope

## Suggested File Touch List

- `src/lib/openfort-config.tsx`
- `src/components/auth/login.tsx`
- `src/components/header.tsx`
- `src/components/main-layout.tsx`
- `src/components/connectwallet/connect-wallet-modal.tsx`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`
- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- route/layout files needed for auth guards

## Existing Frontend Files That Show The Old Contract

These are the clearest handoff pointers for where the old backend/Particle-era assumptions still leak into the frontend:

- `src/app/api/login/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/challenge/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/balance/route.ts`
- `src/utils/get-access-token.util.ts`
- `src/utils/interceptors.utils.ts`
- `src/services/api.service.ts`

All of the above should be treated as removal candidates unless a new Openfort-based backend call path explicitly replaces them.

## Backend Dependency Summary

`backpro` already has:

- JWT access tokens
- refresh-token cookie flow
- auth middleware
- session / lockout logic
- tests and clean layering

But it is still provider-bound to Particle:

- login/register expect `uuid` + `token`
- auth service calls `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- users are keyed around `ParticleID`
- wallet creation depends on Particle user info

# v0.2.1 Openfort Backend Migration Part 1

**Date:** 2026-03-27  
**Status:** Approved plan  
**Frontend companion:** `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`

## Goal

Migrate `backpro` from Particle-based authentication to an Openfort-compatible backend session model while preserving the existing JWT, refresh-token, and middleware architecture.

## Current Backend Reality

`backpro` already has a good authentication foundation:

- JWT access token generation
- refresh-token cookie flow
- auth middleware
- session and lockout handling
- tests and clean layering

But it is still tied to Particle:

- login/register inputs expect `uuid` + `token`
- auth service calls `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- users are keyed around `ParticleID`
- wallet creation depends on Particle user info

## Selected Direction

- Create and use branch `openfort`
- Preserve the existing session architecture
- Replace Particle as the identity/auth provider
- Add a minimal protected API surface needed by the frontend
- Treat PR #18 as selective reference material for later KYC work
- There are no legacy users to migrate, so the backend may make direct schema/contract changes on `openfort` instead of preserving Particle compatibility

## Repo Relationship / Handoff Context

- This repo is the backend half of the migration.
- The frontend half lives in the sibling repo: `../front-pro`
- Backend task document: `backpro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-backend-migration-part-1.md`
- Frontend companion document: `front-pro/docs-dev/tasks/v0.2.1-openfort-implementation-part-2.md`
- If work stops here, resume from the `openfort` branch in both repositories.

## Current Branch Policy

- `backpro/openfort` is the branch of record for backend migration work
- `backpro/develop` remains the pre-Openfort backend line
- `front-pro/openfort` is the branch of record for frontend migration work
- `front-pro/develop` was intentionally reset to the Particle-era fallback point `0dd88faefa2aa875f73d26fd0dba55c7e145adff`

## Current Active Auth Contract

Current routed auth endpoints in `backpro`:

- `/v1/auth/register`
- `/v1/auth/login`
- `/v1/auth/refresh`
- `/v1/auth/logout`

Current request/response behavior:

- register/login expect Particle-style `uuid` + `token`
- successful login returns:
  - JWT `access_token`
  - refresh-token cookie

## Recommended Replacement Auth Contract

Replace the Particle pair (`uuid` + `token`) with a single Openfort session-token exchange:

- `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
  - required header: `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>`
  - token is sourced on the frontend from `await useUser().getAccessToken()`
  - optional body: only app-specific profile fields that Openfort does not own
- `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - unchanged in purpose; continues to mint a new InfraFund access token from the refresh cookie
- `POST /v1/auth/logout`
  - unchanged in purpose; revokes the InfraFund session
- `GET /v1/me`
  - first authenticated read endpoint for the app shell

Validation rule for `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`:

- do not trust frontend-supplied user IDs or emails
- verify the presented Openfort access token against Openfort server-side first
- derive the durable external identity from the validated Openfort session response (`user.id`)
- then create or look up the local InfraFund user and issue the existing InfraFund JWT + refresh cookie

Official Openfort guidance for server-side validation points to session verification via Openfort's server APIs (`getSession`). Since `backpro` is Go, implement an Openfort adapter in Go that performs the same server-side session validation over HTTPS; do not rely on client-side JWT parsing alone.

## Primary Backend Entry Points To Rework

These are the most important implementation handoff files:

- `internal/interfaces/rest/router/auth.go`
- `internal/interfaces/rest/handler/auth.go`
- `internal/interfaces/rest/input/auth.go`
- `internal/application/auth/auth.go`
- `internal/application/auth/auth_helpers.go`
- `internal/application/auth/dto/login.go`
- `internal/application/auth/dto/registeration.go`
- `internal/domain/user/entity/user.go`
- `internal/domain/user/repository/user.go`
- `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/user_repo.go`
- `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/queries/user.sql`

Particle-specific anchors to remove or redesign:

- `ParticleID` field on user entities / persistence
- `GetByParticleID(...)`
- `ExistsParticleID(...)`
- `particle.GetUserInfo(...)` in auth service
- wallet creation during auth based on Particle wallet payloads

## Target Outcome

1. `backpro` no longer depends on Particle for login/register
2. `backpro` still issues JWT access tokens and refresh-token cookies
3. The frontend can exchange Openfort-authenticated identity for an InfraFund app session
4. The backend exposes first authenticated endpoints such as `/me` and account/KYC status
5. Future KYC work can build on a stable post-Particle auth model

## Greenfield Schema Decision

Because there are no existing users to migrate:

- rename/replace `particle_id` with `openfort_user_id` as the unique durable identity key
- remove `GetByParticleID(...)` / `ExistsParticleID(...)` repository methods in favor of Openfort equivalents
- delete Particle-specific DTO fields from login/register handlers
- allow the schema and endpoint contract to break cleanly on `openfort`

Because the current frontend no longer collects a registration profile before login:

- first successful Openfort exchange should auto-provision a minimal local user
- use `openfort_user_id` as the only required external identity
- default role to `investor`
- default status to `pending_kyc`
- either make `type` nullable or supply a temporary default during auto-provisioning; do not keep auth blocked on the old Particle-era registration payload

For this branch, the recommended choice is to simplify the schema enough for auto-provisioning instead of recreating a separate registration form before users can enter the app.

## Wallet Data Decision

Do not preserve the old Particle behavior where backend auth creates wallet rows as part of login/register.

- Openfort owns wallet lifecycle
- wallet balances/pages are expected to read directly from chain/Openfort client state in the frontend
- backend auth should not fail just because no wallet sync occurred
- any wallet persistence in `backpro` should be a later sync concern, not a prerequisite for authentication

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1 — Define the new auth contract

- Replace the Particle-specific auth input contract
- Use `Authorization: Bearer <openfort_access_token>` as the proof of identity sent from the frontend
- Validate that token against Openfort server-side before issuing InfraFund credentials
- Keep the backend-issued session model rather than making the frontend trust-only
- Add `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange` as the new entry point

### Phase 2 — Replace Particle-bound auth logic

- Remove auth service dependency on `particle.GetUserInfo(...)`
- Replace `ParticleID`-centric lookup / registration assumptions
- Use `openfort_user_id` as the durable user identity key and mapping strategy
- Stop requiring Particle wallet payloads during auth

### Phase 3 — Preserve and adapt existing session architecture

- Keep JWT access token generation
- Keep refresh-token cookie flow
- Keep auth middleware and session management
- Rework only the identity acquisition and validation layer

### Phase 4 — Add minimal authenticated API surface

- Add `/me` or equivalent current-account endpoint
- Add basic account-status endpoint(s)
- Add KYC status endpoint(s) if that is the first protected product need

At the time of writing, those account/KYC surfaces are not present in the active router and must be added explicitly.

### Phase 5 — Frontend handshake integration

- Align the new backend auth contract with the `front-pro` Openfort flow
- Expect the frontend to send the Openfort access token obtained from `useUser().getAccessToken()`
- Expect the frontend to call `backpro` directly with `credentials: 'include'`
- Replace the old frontend proxy assumptions that expected Particle-era backend auth

### Phase 6 — KYC follow-up

- Review PR #18 selectively
- Reuse only the parts that fit the new auth contract cleanly
- Do not merge the PR wholesale without additional review

## PR Notes

### PR #18

- open draft PR
- useful Sumsub / applicant groundwork
- not merge-ready
- relevant later, not a direct Openfort auth solution
- status from review: draft + dirty, so treat it as source material, not a merge target during auth migration

Useful parts of PR #18 to revisit later:

- Sumsub adapter groundwork
- applicant service / persistence groundwork
- KYC applicant migration work

But note: active router integration for those KYC flows does not appear to be merged into the current branch line.

### PR #22

- unrelated to Openfort migration
- scheduler test race-condition fix only

## Expected Areas to Touch

- auth input / DTO definitions
- auth service and related tests
- user identity mapping logic
- Openfort session-validation adapter/client
- middleware / session integration points as needed
- first authenticated account endpoints
- docs for the new auth contract

## Validation / Environment Notes

- A full local `go test ./...` run is currently **not clean in this environment**, for reasons that appear pre-existing and unrelated to this documentation work:
  - missing generated package `internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres/gen`
  - missing `tests/mocks`
  - `sonic` build issue in the current environment
- Treat those as baseline setup blockers to resolve before or during backend implementation.

## Effort Estimate

- backend auth migration only: roughly **3–5 focused days**
- add first protected account endpoints: **+2–3 days**
- selective KYC follow-up from PR #18: **additional several days to ~1 week**

## Execution Order

1. establish backend planning docs
2. migrate auth contract away from Particle
3. add minimal protected account endpoints
4. integrate with `front-pro`
5. evaluate KYC follow-up from PR #18

## Recommended First Code Pass After This Doc

1. add an Openfort session-validation adapter and `POST /v1/auth/openfort/exchange`
2. replace `particle_id` with `openfort_user_id` through entity/repository/sql layers
3. remove wallet creation from the auth path
4. preserve JWT + refresh-cookie issuance
5. add `/me` endpoint
